summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn continued the Changed series with part two, Change My Heart. The service opened with a testimony from a couple who described how a slow drift away from God led them into a double life and addiction, and how God brought them freedom, sobriety, and a new peace in Christ. Pastor Travis then used the picture of a caterpillar becoming a butterfly to show that God does not simply improve us. He makes us new, as 2 Corinthians 5:17 declares. The church also read a declaration together, giving God full access to change their minds, hearts, habits, and relationships.

Using an apple tree illustration, Pastor Travis explained that fruit reveals the root. Many of us try to attach better fruit to a root that has never been healed, managing behavior while ignoring what drives it. Citing Matthew 7:18, he taught that real change begins in the heart. King David's prayer in Psalm 51:10 was held up as a model: David asked God for a clean heart rather than a better reputation or easier circumstances. Pastor Travis also recalled Jesus' question, "Do you want to be healed?" and invited listeners to honestly consider whether they are willing to give God full access.

He shared four truths about the heart. First, the heart is the source of our problems, so the fruit we see points to a deeper root. Second, the heart can drift without our noticing. Drawing on Matthew 15:8, the story of Judas, Elijah's challenge on Mount Carmel, and Jesus' words to the lukewarm, he cautioned that nearness to church is not the same as surrender, and that a divided heart leads to a weary life. Jeremiah 17:9 and Proverbs 3:5 reminded us that our hearts can deceive us, so we trust the Lord rather than our own understanding. Third, the heart follows what we treasure (Matthew 6:21). He described an idol as anything we love, trust, desire, fear, or value more than God, and used the rich young ruler to show how even good things can take God's place. Fourth, God wants to give us a new heart, as promised in Ezekiel 36:26. The gospel is not behavior modification but heart transformation, and no one can perform their way into it. We need a Savior.

The message closed with an extended time of prayer at the altar, a prayer of surrender and salvation, and worship. Pastor Travis encouraged anyone who gave their life to Christ to reach out through the QR code, reminding the church that we were never meant to follow Jesus alone.
mainPoints: Real change happens at the root, not the fruit: the heart is the source of our problems, and it can drift or deceive us without our noticing.
Our hearts follow what we treasure, so we must honestly name and surrender any idol that competes with God for first place.
The good news is heart transformation, not behavior modification: we cannot perform our way into change, but God gives a new heart to those who surrender to Jesus.

Monday.scripture: Ezekiel 36:26: I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit in you; I will remove from you your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
Monday.focus: Giving God full access to your heart.
Monday.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes. Write down a few words that describe your heart's condition today (for example weary, hopeful, guarded, or distracted), then read the verse out loud over those words.
Monday.prayer: Lord, I give you access to my heart today. Soften what has grown hard and make me new from the inside out. In Jesus' name, amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Matthew 7:18: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.
Tuesday.focus: Looking beneath the fruit to the root.
Tuesday.action: Pick one habit or reaction you keep repeating. Write down what you think might be underneath it (such as fear, pride, or an old hurt), and bring that root to God in prayer instead of only trying to manage the behavior.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, show me the root behind the fruit in my life. Heal what is hidden and help me trust you with it. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Matthew 6:21: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
Wednesday.action: Look over your calendar and spending from the past week. Ask honestly what they say about what you value most, then choose one small change that puts God first, such as scheduling time in the Word or giving generously.
Wednesday.prayer: Jesus, be first in my time, my money, and my attention. Align my treasure with your heart. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Matthew 22:37: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.
Thursday.focus: Surrendering anything that competes with God.
Thursday.action: Ask God to show you one thing you have been unwilling to lay down (a good thing that became a God thing). Write it on a note, pray over it, and take one concrete step of surrender today.
Thursday.prayer: Lord, I want to love you with all my heart. I lay down what I have held too tightly. Be on the throne of my life. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Psalm 51:10: Create in me a pure heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.
Friday.focus: Honest repentance and guarding against drift.
Friday.action: Pray Psalm 51:10 out loud. Confess to God any small compromise or distraction that has pulled you away from him, and consider sharing your commitment to stay close to Jesus with a trusted believer who can encourage you.
Friday.prayer: God, forgive me for the ways I have drifted. Create in me a clean heart and keep me close to you. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Romans 1:16: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes.
Saturday.focus: Living boldly and walking with others.
Saturday.action: Thank God for the change he is doing in you. Then encourage one person this weekend, either by sharing something God is doing in your life or by inviting them to watch this series or join you at church.
Saturday.prayer: Jesus, thank you for the cross and for new life. Give me courage to live boldly for you and to walk with your people. Amen.

title: How to Change What’s Really Controlling Your Life | Change My Heart
